title: GPU regional growth sprint plan 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures the projected GPU capacity needs for Hosted/Dedicated/Private across NA, EU, and APAC for CY2026, the incremental sprint-level rollout timeline, procurement notes, utilization assumptions, and immediate action items for the next three sprints. Use this as the canonical operational ask for infra planning until we lock numbers in the Q1 commit review.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Net new baseline request for 2026: +1,200 A100-80GB equivalent GPUs distributed NA: 50%, EU: 30%, APAC: 20%.
- Primary drivers: Hosted API 2x growth in conversational usage, Dedicated customer onboarding (5 large committed customers), APAC pilot for lower-latency regional routing.
- Risk focus: APAC spot capacity volatility and EU procurement lead time for reserved pools.

Assumptions and equivalencies (shared):
- Unit = A100 80GB equivalent (quantization/softer GPUs normalized).
- Average utilization target for steady-state: 65% across regions (we plan headroom for spikes).
- Batching and KV-cache improvements from Optimize expected to reduce peak token-cost by ~10% starting 2026-Q2.
- On-demand vs reserved mix: target 70% reserved for Dedicated pools, 30% burst on-demand for Hosted.

Notes on the table: numbers are conservative requests from product + solutions teams and include a 15% safety buffer over raw model compute needs. We normalize to A100-80GB; conversion factors for other instance types are attached in the procurement ticket.

Rollout timeline (high level milestones):
- 2025-12-01: Finalize Q1 reserved purchase draft (INFRA-4321 owner: Miguel Santos).
- 2026-01-15: Provision NA canary cluster (us-west1, 48 nodes) and run smoke runs with model-family X.
- 2026-02-01: EU reserved pool sizing sign-off; engage legal for cross-border T&Cs for customer MRs.
- 2026-03-01: APAC pilot live (ap-southeast-1) with traffic shifted for 10% of APAC requests.
- 2026-05-15: Dedicated customer onboarding batch-1 (3 customers) in NA/EU.
- 2026-08-01: APAC regional pool scale-up decision point (KPI: p99 latency < 220 ms for chat flows).
- 2026-10-01: Final capacity sync for holiday/peak and reserved contracts for 2027.

Operational triggers and scaling policy (short):
- Autoscale triggers: sustained host utilization > 80% for 12h -> scale reserved by 10% or enable burst-on-demand.
- Fallback policy: if spot capacity < 60% reliability for 48h in a region, route burst to secondary region with traffic limiters and notify SRE.
- Canary rollback: if model p99 latency regresses > 20% during canary, roll back and open postmortem.

Cost and procurement notes (high level):
- Preliminary quoted price band (cloud list, pre-negotiation): A100 equiv reserved ~ $X/day (see Confluence pricing page) — we will attach vendor quotes in linked artifacts.
- Procurement lead time: 4–6 weeks for reserved instance contractual paperwork in EU (longer if custom compliance language required).
- Action: get pricing firm by 2025-12-10 to meet January provisioning.

Risks & mitigations:
- APAC spot churn: mitigation = keep a small reserved anchor + multi-zone placement and pre-warm instances during promo windows.
- EU legal T&Cs blocking reserved marketplace SKU: mitigation = elevate to Legal and Solutions Eng now; draft template available in Confluence page.
- Demand overshoot from new customers: mitigation = throttle onboarding with clear SLAs and use Dedicated burst quotas.

Immediate action items (owners):
1) Miguel Santos — finalize reserved purchase draft and submit INFRA-4321 by 2025-11-25.
2) Lin Zhao — run cost sensitivity sim for 3 model-mix scenarios and attach CSV to this doc by 2025-11-24 (ticket GROWTH-709).
3) Emma Carter — coordinate APAC pilot infra and prepare SRE runbook for spot fallbacks by 2026-01-20.
4) Priya Nair — confirm Dedicated customer contract start dates and expected qps per customer (provide list) by 2025-12-05.
5) Team — sync with #infra-capacity Slack channel daily during provisioning windows; escalate to oncall if autoscale triggers fire twice in 24h during canary.

Open questions (to resolve in next sync):
- Do we increase headroom target from 15% to 20% to account for longer sequence models? (Product + Applied-ML to advise)
- Are there preferred HW SKUs for EU customers that require pinned networking/hostname? (SRE / Networking)
- Should we front-load additional APAC capacity if early latency tests pass to avoid multi-phase procurement? (Finance input on cost).
